items.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I was on a band once where I was the only white kid in the band. There was Jonah Jones on trumpet, Coleman Hawkins on tenor, Benny Green on trombone, Jo Jones on drums, various bass players, Gene Ramey maybe on bass and myself, the young white hope.

ctx.x: I don’t see many young black players coming up. Now there seems to be a lot of younger white guys who are a generation below you I guess that are embracing the style. And I’m wondering why.

It’s very sad. I’m very sorry to hear that because as I was saying, years ago when I played this music I was a young kid. And a lot of young kids, there was Johnny Windhurst, Bob Wilber, Kenny Davern, a young crop of musicians playing and we’d be playing with mixed bands like crazy. I mean I’d be — I was on a band once where I was the only white kid in the band. There was Jonah Jones on trumpet, Coleman Hawkins on tenor, Benny Green on trombone, Jo Jones on drums, various bass players, Gene Ramey maybe on bass…
I think it’s a good opinion.
